analysis.title: JPM Tech Sketch Special Edition: Schilsky's Q326 Earnings Preview Bonanza (GOOGL, META, AMZN, NFLX, SPOT, ETSY)
key_insights: Mark Schilsky's special edition previews Q326 earnings for GOOGL, META, AMZN, NFLX, SPOT and ETSY. Each preview lists the Street number and the buyside 'bogey' (the level investors actually expect).

GOOGL (reports Wed Oct 28 after the close): Google Cloud is expected to beat on TPU sales. Search is expected to miss the Street by about 100 bps because of alt data. Schilsky says to focus on the 2027 revenue and earnings ramp, not a small Search miss.
GOOGL Search: investors expect about +14% Y/Y against a Street of about +15.0%. A beat would likely send the stock higher the next day, because the market already assumes a miss.

GOOGL Cloud: Street growth is about +90% Y/Y and investors expect +105% to +115%. Implied TPU sales in the quarter are $5B to $7B. Schilsky calls Cloud EBIT margin the most important KPI, with the Street at about 33%. A beat would partly validate that TPU margins match or exceed core Cloud margins.

GOOGL Operating income: Street is about $43B and the buyside bogey is about $45B. For 2027, Street Cloud growth of +68% is seen as too low (investors say +100% to +120%), and Street capex of about $305B is below investor views of $330B to $350B.

GOOGL valuation: investors are expected to capitalize TPU earnings at about 15x (an NVDA/AVGO-like multiple) and core GOOGL EPS at about 20x. That gives a blended P/E in the high teens. 2027 EPS: investors $14.50 to $16.00 vs Street about $15. 2028 EPS: investors $18 to $25 (modal low $20s) vs Street about $18.

META (reports Wed Oct 21 after the close): the stock is up nearly 40% off the lows on Muse and Wonder, and sentiment is very strong. The bogey for Q3 revenue is about $64B (+26% Y/Y FXN) against the $61B to $64B guide and a Street of about $63.25B. Investors want hard Muse KPIs such as DAUs.

META Q426 and 2027 guidance: investors expect a Q4 revenue guide of $72B to $75B against a Street of about $73.5B. For 2027 opex, Street is about $203B and investors expect a guide topping out at $220B to $225B, if one is given at all. 2026 opex guidance should rise about $10B on the AG settlement.
META 2027 capex: Street is about $200B and investors expect $225B to $250B. Schilsky says to watch the sum of 2027 opex and capex, with buyside consensus of $435B to $475B (midpoint $455B).

META equity raise: a majority of investors still expect a raise after Q3 if the stock is high enough (above $800, ideally about $850). 2027 Street EPS of $34 could fall to about $32 on a heavy opex guide. Bulls focus on 2028 EPS of $35 to $45 (majority low $40s) vs Street about $39.

AMZN (reports mid-week of Oct 26 after the close): Schilsky sees Street 2027 AWS growth (about +35% to +37%) as too low given capex. The setup is a widely expected beat-and-raise, which is part of why the stock is not working. Other overhangs are a weak US consumer, AMZN's block of META Muse from its site, and a lack of intra-quarter catalysts.

AMZN Q326: AWS bogey is +42% Y/Y vs Street +37%. Total revenue is expected at $202B to $203B vs guide of $197B to $202B. Operating income bogey is about $28B vs guide of $22.5B to $26.5B and Street $26B.

AMZN Q426 and 2027: investors expect a Q4 revenue guide of $239B to $246B (Street $244.5B) and an operating income guide of $30B to $35B (Street $33B). Leo costs are re-capitalized in Q4, a roughly $1B tailwind. 2027 capex: investors $330B to $350B vs Street just over $280B. 2027 EPS: investors $11.50 to $12.50 vs Street about $11. A Prime price increase is due, with the last US one in Q122.

NFLX (reported Tue Oct 20 after the close): it enters as the most crowded short in Internet and Media, with engagement as the debate. Nobody expects a beat and raise. Bogey for revenue is +11% Y/Y FXN in line with guide, and operating margin is about 33.5% vs guide 33.2% and Street 33.1%.

NFLX guidance: investors will not tolerate a downtick from about +12% Q4 and full-year 2026 revenue growth. Q4 operating margin guide is about 27.5% and the full year is 31.5%. The real debate is 2027, where bears see revenue growth below 10% and bulls see +11% or better. Timing of the next US price increase (possibly July 2027 on a 15-month cadence) is a swing factor.

SPOT (reports Thu Oct 22 before the open): the stock is stuck in a $450 to $550 range since the May Investor Day and is down 9% YTD. It needs a clean quarter and new products or tiers. The AI remixing product is now mostly seen as a Q127 launch, pending WMG and SONY licensing deals.

SPOT Q326 and Q426: MAU bogey is +13m to +14m Q/Q vs Street +11m, premium subs bogey is +6m vs Street +5m, and gross margin bogey is 33.1% to 33.2% vs guide of 32.9%. Gross margin is the key Q4 KPI. Investors expect a guide of 33.6% to 33.7% while Street is about 33.7% (earlier 33.9%).
SPOT/NFLX pair: Schilsky says long SPOT, short NFLX remains a very popular pair trade and he endorses it.

ETSY (reports Wed Oct 28 before the open): the stock is up 54% YTD. GMS bogey is +7% Y/Y or a touch higher vs a guide of +4% to +6% and a Street of about +5.5%. Bears say more than 100% of GMS growth comes from AOV rather than orders, and Active Buyers fell 40 bps Y/Y in Q226.

ETSY buyback and Q426: a new $2B repurchase program was authorized Aug 3 after the roughly $1.4B Depop sale to EBAY, and investors hope for many hundreds of millions repurchased in Q3 vs $250m in Q226. Investors expect a Q4 GMS guide no worse than +4% to +6% Y/Y vs a Street of +4%, despite a comp that is 250 bps harder.
JPM analyst views cited: Doug upgraded META to Buy and raised AMZN AWS estimates in a revisions note. Bryan is bullish on ETSY. Doug expects an in-line SPOT 3Q with Q4 gross margin below consensus.

market_movers.rationale: JPM's Doug upgraded META to Buy, citing early-stage release of frontier models and AI products beyond advertising, including the Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access.
Bryan's JPM view is bullish and expects solid results and continued GMS outperformance. Schilsky flags AOV-driven growth and weak buyer metrics as the bear case.
Cloud revenue is expected to beat on TPU sales and a Search beat would likely lift the stock, while a small Search miss is already expected.
Schilsky calls NFLX the most crowded short in Internet and expects any post-print pop to be short-lived without 2027 revenue and margin color.

sector_views.rationale: Positioning is mixed. NFLX is a crowded short, SPOT, AMZN and CVNA are frustrating crowded longs, and ETSY could become a crowded short. Investors are focused on 2027 capex, opex and AI monetization.

earnings_insights: GOOGL Q326 (reports 10/28 after close, estimates): Search growth Street about +15.0% Y/Y vs investor about +14% (range +13.5% to +15.0%), YouTube Street +11% Y/Y, Google Cloud growth Street about +90% Y/Y vs investor +105% to +115%, Cloud EBIT margin Street about 33%, operating income Street about $43B vs investor bogey about $45B.

META Q326 (reports 10/21 after close, estimates): revenue Street about $63.25B vs investor bogey about $64B (+26% Y/Y FXN), guide $61B to $64B. Q426 revenue Street about $73.5B (about +24% Y/Y FXN), investors expect a guide of $72B to $75B.

AMZN Q326 (reports week of 10/26 after close, estimates): AWS growth Street +37% Y/Y vs investor +42%, total revenue Street $202B vs investor $202B to $203B, operating income Street $26B vs investor about $28B, guide $22.5B to $26.5B. Q426 revenue Street $244.5B and operating income Street $33B.

NFLX Q326 (reported 10/20 after close, estimates, not actuals): revenue growth in line at +11% Y/Y FXN, operating margin guide 33.2% vs Street 33.1% (Bloomberg) vs investor bogey 33.5%. Q4 revenue growth guide about +12% Y/Y FXN, Q4 operating margin implied about 27.5% vs Street 27.7%, 2026 operating margin guide 31.5% vs Street 31.7%. Q226: stock fell 7% on the print after UCAN revenue missed.

SPOT Q326 (reports 10/22 before open, estimates): MAUs guide implied vs Street +11m Q/Q, investor bogey +13m to +14m, premium subs guide +5m vs investor +6m, gross margin guide 32.9% vs investor 33.1% to 33.2%. Q426: MAUs Street about +30m, premium subs Street about +10m, gross margin Street about 33.7%.

ETSY Q326 (reports 10/28 before open, estimates): GMS guide +4% to +6% Y/Y, Street about +5.5%, investor bogey +7%. Q226 reported Active Buyers -40 bps Y/Y and $250m of buybacks. Q426 GMS Street +4% Y/Y.

trade_ideas.description: Pair trade: long SPOT, short NFLX
trade_ideas.rationale: SPOT trades at a premium to NFLX, NFLX has de-rated 25% YTD on engagement worries, and the author says the pair is very popular and endorsed.

risk_factors: GOOGL: Search revenue could miss the Street by more than the expected 100 bps, and TPU margins may fall short of core Cloud margins.
META: a 2027 opex guide above expectations could cut Street 2027 EPS of $34 toward $32. Muse monetization may not be meaningful until 2028.
AMZN: widely expected beat-and-raise limits upside, a struggling US consumer weighs on Retail, and management may not answer the AI agent strategy question well.
NFLX: slow engagement growth could cut subscriber growth and pricing power, and 2027 revenue growth could dip below 10%.
SPOT: delay of the AI remixing product, pending WMG and SONY licensing deals, and a Q4 gross margin guide below Street.
ETSY: growth driven by AOV rather than orders, with declining Active Buyers and a harder 2-year comp.
vol_and_positioning: NFLX is described as the most crowded short in Internet and Media. The stock is near its lows of the year and investors expect no beat and raise, so a squeeze is possible if it merely meets Street revenue and margin estimates.
SPOT, AMZN, CVNA and TTWO are described as a frustrating crowded-long group that draws the most complaints when it underperforms.
ETSY could become a crowded short if investors conclude the 2-year GMS stack is peaking or orders keep declining.
Long SPOT, short NFLX is described as a very popular pair trade that the author endorses.
META: a majority of investors expect an equity raise after Q3 if the stock is high enough, citing a level above $800 and ideally about $850.

tension_points.bull_case: Google Cloud revenue is set to beat on TPU sales and could equal Search revenue by late 2028. Investors expect Cloud growth of +105% to +115% vs Street ~+90%, and a bigger 2027 earnings ramp.
tension_points.bear_case: Search growth is expected to miss the Street's ~+15.0% Y/Y by about 100 bps on alt data, and the stock has languished since Q2 earnings.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Search miss deeper than the expected 100 bps, or Cloud EBIT margin below the Street's ~33%, which would suggest TPU margins are lower than core Cloud margins.

tension_points.bull_case: Muse and Wonder have driven a ~40% rally off the lows, and 2028 Muse monetization could lift EPS to $35 to $45 vs Street ~$39. A buy upgrade cites frontier models and AI products.
tension_points.bear_case: Street 2027 opex of ~$203B is about $18B too light, so 2027 EPS of $34 could fall to about $32. Muse monetization may be small in 2027 and an equity raise is possible.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 2027 opex guide above the $220B to $225B high end, or no Muse KPIs or operating income commentary on the call.

tension_points.bull_case: Sentiment is very weak and the stock is near its yearly lows, so meeting Street revenue and margin could trigger a squeeze. Bulls see 2027 revenue growth of ~+11% or better.
tension_points.bear_case: Engagement is weak, management admits it is not growing as fast as it wants, and bears see 2027 revenue growth below 10% and a funding-short setup.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Any downtick from the ~+12% Q4 and full-year 2026 FXN revenue growth guide, or a US price increase later than the expected July 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: GMS growth is accelerating, the stock is up 54% YTD, and an accelerated buyback follows the Depop sale proceeds of about $1.4B.
tension_points.bear_case: Alt data suggests more than 100% of GMS growth comes from AOV rather than orders, Active Buyers fell 40 bps Y/Y in Q226, and comps are getting harder.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further deterioration in Active Buyers or a Q426 GMS guide below +4% to +6% Y/Y, which would embolden shorts.

theme_stances.evidence: All eyes are on 2027 – especially the Opex guide

theme_stances.key_argument: Slow engagement growth is seen as a harbinger of lower subscriber growth and pricing power, so any post-print pop is likely short-lived.
